title: Journal of a Residence of Two Years and a Half in Great Britain
short_title: Journal of a Residence in Great Britain
summary: Jehangeer Nowrojee and his cousin Hirjeebhoy Merwanjee were young assistant shipbuilders at the East India Company’s dockyard in Bombay, members of the Parsi family that had built ships there since 1735. Sent by their family to learn how steam vessels were designed, they sailed from Bombay in March 1838 by the Cape of Good Hope and St. Helena, spent two and a half years in England and Scotland, and wrote this book in London in April 1841, before going home.

It is arranged by subject rather than by date: the voyage; London’s conveyances, exhibitions, theatres, museums, hospitals, markets, Parliament and courts; their training at Chatham dockyard and the launches they saw there; visits to Sheerness, Woolwich, Windsor and Egham; a tour of the dockyards and manufacturing towns from Portsmouth and Plymouth to Bristol, Birmingham, Liverpool and Glasgow; newspapers, customs, the climate, and verses written in their albums. The authors say they wrote it chiefly for Indians who might visit England.
